$comment: Riftlight, Forgotten Paths key node (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, reading-room; design note memory-paths-continuity-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 to the pilot's bar. Question: has this river ever run here before? Elder Murmur carries it; Flurry (who will keep the next reading room) has the stake; Pip Thistledown voices Lady Olivia's ideas. The p1 (old_river) is the Paths fragment: the memory ice shows the river leaving by a different valley; Murmur's warning follows in deep_sound. Sets fragment_paths_learned on every path; reads valley_crossed_high and fragment_coast_learned.
title: The River in the Memory Ice

goal.text: Ask the yetis' memory ice: has this river ever run here before?

steps.label: Go down into the reading room
See what the old ice remembers
Prove it is the same river

plate.narration: Deep in the glacier, yeti hands have carved a room from blue ice. Lantern light slides along the walls. Some of the ice shines with pictures too faint to read.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Everyone whispers in the reading room, so a loud noise is an event. The memory ice is witnessed, never explained. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Elder Murmur: Elder Murmur, the very old yeti who keeps the reading room (she/her). Whispers everything, even her jokes. Slow as a snowdrift, never hurries and never guesses. Drinks her tea with ice in it and blows on it to make it colder. Wants to read the memory ice without waking it.
npcVoices.Flurry: Flurry, a young yeti keeper (she/her). Quick, nervous and kind. Knits little striped hats for icicles. Will keep the new reading room the builders are carving, and worries a moving river might come into it.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants a copy of the memory ice to impress her. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.

arrival.narration: The upper path ends at a round door cut into the glacier, clear as a bottle. A very old yeti opens it before you knock. She wears three scarves and holds a cup of tea with ice in it. "Elder Murmur," she whispers. "I keep the reading room. Today you crossed a river in a valley that was dry. Has this river ever run here before? Our memory ice may know. Come and ask it with me."

pip_here.narration: Inside, Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, is already waiting with his notebook open. "Lady Olivia says memory ice is the oldest map in the world," he says, much too loudly. Murmur puts a finger to her lips. "I'm going to copy it for her," Pip whispers.

variants.text: Murmur looks at your dry boots. "You crossed high, over the rocks. Good. High eyes see the shape of a valley."
Murmur looks at your wet boots. "You crossed low, by the water. Good. Wet knees remember how a river pulls."

stair.narration: A stair spirals down into the ice. Every step squeaks like a mouse if you stomp. "Quiet feet," Murmur whispers. "The old ice listens." Pip pats a tea tray on a string. "Or we slide! Lady Olivia says the fastest way down is the best way." How will you go down?

choices.label: Slide down on Pip's tea tray
Glide down the middle of the spiral

check_tiptoe.narration: Toes first. Heels never. "Ninety-nine steps," Murmur whispers. "I counted them once."
check_tiptoe.prompt: Tiptoe all the way down without one squeak

onSuccess.narration: Not one squeak. At the bottom Murmur nods at you, which for a yeti is a very big compliment.

onFailure.narration: Step ninety squeaks. So do ninety-one and ninety-two, because you slip and bump down the rest on your bottom. Murmur winces. Far below, the ice gives a long, low creak.

check_sled.narration: The tea tray is very fast. Pip is already going. "Dig your heels in to stop!" he calls back.
check_sled.prompt: Dig in your heels and stop the tray before the wall

onSuccess.narration: You scrape to a stop one whisker from the wall. Pip claps, very quietly, with his paws in his mittens.

onFailure.narration: You do not stop. The tray hits the bottom wall with a BONG, like a giant spoon on a pot. The whole room hums. Murmur closes her eyes. Far below, the ice gives a long, low creak.

glide.narration: Your griffin spreads its wings and floats down the middle of the spiral, round and round, like a falling leaf. Not one squeak. Pip slides down after you on the tea tray and writes GRIFFINS: QUIET in his notebook.

room.narration: The reading room is round and glassy and very quiet. Yeti readers in blankets stare into the walls. Inside the ice, pictures move, faint as breath on a window: falling snow, a bird, a goat chewing. "Memory ice," Murmur whispers. "It keeps what it saw when it froze. We read it. We never make it show."

variants.text: Tonight the pictures shiver and blur. The readers look up at you, and then down at the floor, where the creak came from.

tuft.narration: A young yeti hurries over with a little striped hat. "This is Flurry," Murmur whispers. "She will keep our new reading room, when the builders finish carving it." Flurry points at an icicle dripping onto a stack of slates, a hundred years of the readers' notes. "The hat is for the icicle. Help me? And then ask the old ice if rivers can move. What if one moves into my new room?"

choices.label: Stack the stools and put the hat on

check_icicle.narration: Three stools, one on top of another. Flurry holds the bottom one. Pip holds his breath.
check_icicle.prompt: Stack the stools so they stay steady, then climb up and hat the icicle

onSuccess.narration: The little striped hat slides on. The icicle stops dripping at once. Flurry claps her mittens. "It suits it!" She looks at you as if you might be very good at things.

onFailure.narration: The top stool wobbles, and you come down holding the hat and a lot of air. Flurry catches you, mostly. She hats the icicle herself, standing on her toes. "Thank you for trying," she says, kindly.

snap_icicle.narration: SNAP. The icicle comes off clean, and no more drips fall on the slates. But the snap rings around the whole room. The readers jump. The pictures in the walls go cloudy, like a breath on glass. Flurry looks at the little hat in her paws. "Well," Murmur whispers. "It won't drip now."

ask_wall.narration: Murmur points to the back of the room. "The old wall is through there, the oldest ice we can read. My knees cannot go anymore. Bring me what it shows." A low tunnel runs that way, dripping. Above it runs a narrow ledge hung with lamps. How will you get there?

drips.narration: Cold drops fall from the tunnel roof: plip, plip, plip. Crawl on between them. A drop down the neck makes anybody yelp. Pip crawls behind you with his notebook in his teeth.

onSuccess.narration: You come out the far end dry as toast. Pip gets one drop right on the nose, and is much too proud to yelp.

onFailure.narration: A drop lands right down the back of your neck.

onAssisted.narration: Pip counts the drips out loud, very softly, and you crawl on every "now." You come out dry as toast.

yelp.narration: You yelp. The tunnel yelps back: yelp, yelp, yelp, all the way to the old wall. The ice ahead turns cloudy. "Sorry," you whisper. "Sorry, sorry," says the tunnel. Pip pats your back.

check_ledge.narration: The ledge is as wide as a loaf of bread. You hold on to the lamp hooks and pull yourself along. "Tails up," Pip whispers, holding his high.
check_ledge.prompt: Pull yourself along the ledge without bumping one lamp

onSuccess.narration: Hook, hook, hook. You swing past every lamp, and not one wobbles.

onFailure.narration: Your elbow taps a lamp. It swings, and swings, and drops.

lamp_fall.narration: You catch it, mostly. The glass cracks, and the glow-moss inside goes dim. Now there is one less light at the old wall, and the ice ahead looks cloudier. Pip pats your shoulder. "Lady Olivia says every scientist breaks one thing a day."

listening_floor.narration: Near the old wall is a hole in the floor, no wider than a bucket. Far, far down, somebody is singing the low song from the yetis' singing hall. Pip picks up a pebble. "Lady Olivia says you find out how deep a hole is by dropping something in."

choices.label: Lie down and listen to the song

pebble_drop.narration: Plink. Plink. Plonk. The pebble falls for a long, long time. Then, far below, the singing stops. The floor gives a little creak, and the old wall ahead goes cloudy. Pip counts on his claws. "Very deep," he reports, in a very small voice.

hall_song.narration: You lie flat and listen. The song comes up slow: a long note, a rest, a long note. Your breathing slows to match it. "I could sleep here," Pip mumbles, and nearly does. Now you know the old ice's rhythm.

old_wall.narration: The old wall is pale and smooth, like a frozen pond standing on its edge, with one reading lamp hung beside it. Deep inside, something moves, too faint to see. Pip presses his nose to it. "Lady Olivia says rift magic wakes things up! Ring the Listening Chime at it!" Murmur's whisper floats through the ice from the room behind you. "Or wait. Old ice clears if you are still and patient. It takes a long, cold while."

variants.text: Tonight the old wall is cloudy from all the noise. Waiting will be long, and cold.

choices.label: Ring the chime at the ice
The ice is calm tonight: wait for it
Breathe with the hall's slow song
Sing the low song until the ice clears

ring_chime.narration: You lift the Listening Chime and ring it at the wall. TING. The note runs into the ice like a crack of light. All at once the wall flashes bright as noon, and pictures pour across it, fast, much too fast. "Whoa," breathes Pip. Somewhere behind you, Murmur gasps.

wait_slow.narration: Hold the lamp low and still, and breathe slow. Inside the ice, the cloud drifts and thins and thickens. Lift the lamp at the clearest moment.

interaction.cue: Lift the lamp when the ice is clearest.

onSuccess.narration: Slowly, slowly, the cloud thins away, like fog off a pond.

onFailure.narration: You lift too soon, and the cloud swirls back. You wait again, and again. By the time the ice clears, your fingers are numb and your nose is a little frosty.

onAssisted.narration: Pip whispers "now" at the clear moment, and you lift the lamp together. The cloud thins away, like fog off a pond.

wait_long.narration: The old ice takes a long, cold while. The cold creeps up through your boots and into your toes. Hold the lamp low and still, and lift it at the clearest moment. It comes and goes fast.

interaction.cue: Lift the lamp when the ice is clearest.

onSuccess.narration: At last the cloud thins away, like fog off a pond. Your teeth are chattering, but you can see.

onFailure.narration: You miss the clear moment, and wait for the next, and miss that too. By the time the ice clears, everyone is shivering and Pip's whiskers have frost on them.

onAssisted.narration: Pip whispers "now" at the clear moment, and you lift the lamp together. Your teeth are chattering, but the cloud thins away.

wait_knack.narration: You breathe the way the hall's song taught you: a long breath, a rest, a long breath. The cloud inside the ice drifts in time with you. Lift the lamp at the clearest moment.

interaction.cue: Lift the lamp when the ice is clearest.

onSuccess.narration: Breath by breath, the cloud thins away, like fog off a pond. You hardly feel the cold at all.

onFailure.narration: You lose the rhythm and have to find it again. By the time the ice clears, your fingers are numb.

onAssisted.narration: Pip hums the hall's song under his breath, and you lift the lamp on the rest. The cloud thins away.

song_still.narration: Your songkeeper sings the low song the yetis taught you, so low it is almost not a sound at all. The old wall hums back. The cloud inside it thins and clears, like fog lifting off a pond. Pip forgets to write anything down.

old_river.narration: Elder Murmur has come after all, one slow step at a time, and stands behind you. Inside the old wall, a river is running. You know those ridges. It is the river you crossed today. But in the ice, it turns and leaves by a different valley: the one that was dry, the one you crossed. The memory ice shows the river leaving by a different valley. Long, long ago, this river ran there before. "It has been here before," Pip whispers.

variants.text: In the chime's flash the river flickers, bright and fast, like a picture book with the pages flipping.
The river moves slowly and clearly, like a dream you could almost touch.
You have seen something like this before. On the Saltrot, the buried bridge stands over dry mud, where a river ran in an older shape.

deep_sound.narration: Then, far below the floor, something sighs, long and slow, like a giant turning over in bed. The Listening Chime tugs in your pack, down toward the deepest ice, where the glacier is oldest. Pip takes a huge breath, the kind you take before you yell "Hello!" Murmur puts a paw on his shoulder. "Do not shout near the old ice," she whispers. "You don't know what you might wake."

variants.text: The sigh is loud. The chime's ring is still running through the ice, down and down.

hush_pip.narration: Pip nods. Pip understands. Then Pip whispers, "But Lady Olivia says it's rude not to say hello," and fills his chest for the biggest hello of his life.
hush_pip.prompt: Clap a paw over Pip's mouth before he shouts

onSuccess.narration: Mmmf. Pip's hello comes out as a tiny hum into your paw. Far below, the sigh fades away. Pip goes pink to the ears. "Sorry. That was not scientific."

onFailure.narration: Too slow. "Hel..." bounces off every wall before you catch the rest. Far below, the sigh turns into a groan. A crack runs up the old wall, thin as a hair, and icicles rain from the ceiling. One bonks you.

shaking.narration: From the reading room comes a clatter, then Flurry's voice: "The icicles! They're falling on the slates!" Murmur shuffles back, as fast as a yeti her age can go, which is not fast. In front of you, the river in the ice is starting to fade. What first?

choices.label: Copy the river before it fades
Copy it slowly, while the ice stays clear
Run back and save the slates

copy_flash.narration: The picture is fading fast. Watch where the river goes, then draw it in order on Pip's page.

interaction.cue: Watch the river's way, then draw it in order.

onSuccess.narration: You draw as fast as it fades: ridge, rocks, the turn, the other valley. Every line is there.

onFailure.narration: The picture goes out halfway. Your copy has the ridge and the valley, and a blank in the middle where the river turns.

onAssisted.narration: Pip calls out each shape as it fades, and you draw. Every line is there.

copy_steady.narration: The river runs slowly in the clear ice. Watch where it goes, then draw it in order on Pip's page.

interaction.cue: Watch the river's way, then draw it in order.

onSuccess.narration: Ridge, rocks, the turn, the other valley. Your copy is neat and true.

onFailure.narration: The picture fades before you finish. Your copy has the ridge and the valley, and a blank in the middle where the river turns.

onAssisted.narration: Pip calls each shape out as it passes, and you draw. Your copy is neat and true.

slates_broken.narration: By the time you hurry back, it is over. There are icicles everywhere, and three old slates are cracked right across. Flurry is gathering the pieces in her knitting basket. "It's all right," she says, and sniffs. "Mostly all right."

check_slates.narration: You run back into the reading room. Icicles are shaking loose over the slates. The readers' big stone table has legs as thick as tree trunks. Flurry grabs one end.
check_slates.prompt: Lift the stone table over the slates like a roof

onSuccess.narration: Up it goes. Icicles bounce off the table like hail on a tent. When the shaking stops, every slate is safe. Flurry hugs the stack. "Thank you, thank you."

onFailure.narration: The table only lifts halfway. The icicles hit you instead of the slates. Ow. But when the shaking stops, every slate is safe, and so are you, mostly. Flurry hugs the stack.

fading.narration: Then you remember the river. You hurry back to the old wall. The picture is fading, like a drawing left out in the rain. Only a little is left, and it is going fast. Pip already has his pencil out. "Quick! Draw what's left!"

copy_late.narration: The river is almost gone. Watch where it goes, then draw it in order before the picture fades away.

interaction.cue: Watch the river's way, then draw it in order.

onSuccess.narration: You catch it just in time: ridge, rocks, the turn, the other valley. Then the ice goes pale and quiet.

onFailure.narration: It fades before you finish. Your copy has the ridge and the valley, and a blank in the middle where the river turns.

onAssisted.narration: Pip calls each shape out as it fades, and you draw like lightning. Ridge, rocks, the turn, the other valley.

compare.narration: Back in the reading room, Murmur lays your copy on the stone table, beside Pip's sketch of the valley you crossed today. She blows on her tea to make it colder. "Now prove it," she whispers. "Is it the same valley? A reader never guesses."

variants.text: Your copy is clear, every turn of the river in its place.
Your copy has a blank in the middle, right where the river turns.
Behind her, Flurry is still sweeping up icicles and bits of cracked slate.

choices.label: Line up the copy with Pip's sketch
Ask Murmur to read the old wall herself
You saw those ridges from the high rocks
That turn is where the water pulled you
Tell Murmur about the buried bridge

check_match.narration: Pip holds his sketch up to the lamp. You hold your copy behind it. "If the lines meet," Murmur whispers, "it is the same valley."
check_match.prompt: Slide the copy and the sketch around until the ridges meet

onSuccess.narration: The ridges slide together like two halves of a cookie. Same ridges. Same valley. Murmur checks it twice, and nods.

onFailure.narration: The lines will not quite meet. You turn the pages this way and that, and Pip's sketch gets a thumbprint on it.

match_unsure.narration: Murmur takes your copy and Pip's sketch both. "I will read the old wall again myself," she whispers, "every night, until I am sure." Pip's sketch was his present for Lady Olivia. He swallows. "Keep it," he says. "Science first." A few nights later, Murmur is sure.

match_high.narration: You close your eyes and remember the high rocks, with the valley spread out below you like a map. Those ridges. That fork. That turn. "Same valley," you whisper. Murmur checks it twice, and nods. "High eyes see far."

match_low.narration: You put your finger on the turn in the copy. That is where the water grabbed your knees today and tried to pull you along. Same turn. Same pull. Murmur checks it twice, and nods. "Wet knees remember."

old_slates.narration: Flurry brings the slates you saved. Murmur runs a claw down them, one by one. In every slate, for a hundred years, the river runs its usual way. Not once does it leave by the other valley. "So the old wall is older than every slate here," she whispers. "Older than my grandmother's grandmother."

bridge_pattern.narration: You tell Murmur about the buried bridge on the Saltrot: arches over dry mud, with a waterline carved high up, where a river ran in an older shape. Murmur sets down her tea, which she never does. "Two rivers," she whispers, "both remembering an older shape of the land." Pip writes it down twice, to be safe.

matched.narration: So it is true. Long ago, before any reader was born, this river ran down the valley that was dry. Today, for a little while, it tried to go that way again. "Like it remembered," Flurry whispers. Murmur pours iced tea. Pip gulps his and gets brain freeze.

tuft_worry.narration: Flurry twists her knitting into a knot. "If a river remembers the way it used to go, could it come back? Into my new room?" Murmur looks into her tea. She does not know. What do you tell Flurry?

choices.label: Nobody knows, but you'll help her find out
Remind her how brave the icicle hat was

check_tuft.narration: Flurry's ears are flat. Her knitting is a knot. She looks at the door to the builders' tunnel, and then at the floor.
check_tuft.prompt: Help Flurry feel brave enough to go and see her new room

onSuccess.narration: Flurry unknots her knitting, one loop at a time. "Then I'll go and look," she says. "Tomorrow. With my hats."

onFailure.narration: Flurry nods, but she does not look sure. She tucks her knitting under Murmur's stool, and stays very close to it.

tuft_brave.narration: Flurry looks up at the icicle in its little striped hat. It is not dripping. She laughs. "If an icicle can wear a hat, I can go and look at my new room." She unknots her knitting, one loop at a time.

pip_idea.narration: Pip bounces in his seat. "If rivers remember, Lady Olivia could remind them! She could send a river anywhere we like!" Flurry goes pale under her fur. "Anywhere?" Murmur says nothing, and looks at the floor. What do you tell Pip?

variants.text: His own sketch sits on Murmur's shelf now. He keeps looking at it.

choices.label: Rivers aren't ours to send around

pip_wonders.narration: Pip chews his pencil. "Lady Olivia says everything can be used." He looks at Flurry's worried face. Then he writes, very small: "Ask the river first?" Flurry lets out a long breath.

pip_dreams.narration: Pip writes RIVERS!!! in his notebook and underlines it three times. Flurry pulls her knitting into her lap and holds it tight. Murmur whispers, to nobody in particular, "The old ice was not asked either."

rest.narration: The readers make room for you on the warm side of the room, which is the side with the most blankets. "Guests first," Murmur whispers, handing out lichen cakes. They taste like a forest kept in the cold.

variants.text: Flurry lays the cracked slates out on a blanket, piece by piece, like a puzzle she means to finish.
Flurry keeps one paw on the stack of slates you saved, the whole time.
Through the tunnel, the old wall has frosted white from the chime's flash. Nobody can read it again until spring.
Through the tunnel, the old wall is still clear. A reader is already at it, nose to the ice.

choices.label: Ask Murmur what else the old ice has shown her
Help Flurry mend the cracked slates
Help Flurry pack for her new room

murmur_tale.narration: Murmur thinks for a long time. "Once, I saw snow falling up," she whispers. "Once, a bird that flew backward. I wrote them down. I did not write why. A reader writes what she sees." She looks at the floor, where the deep sound came from, and says nothing else.

mend_slates.narration: You fit the cracked slates together with Flurry, edge to edge. A few pieces are missing. Flurry writes the missing words back in from memory, very neatly, with her tongue between her teeth. "Not the same," she says. "But not gone."

tuft_pack.narration: Flurry packs for her new room: one blanket, one stool, eleven icicle hats. "The builders say it's nearly finished," she says. "Way down their tunnel, in the coldest, quietest ice." She wiggles. "They want me to come and see it tomorrow."

way_out.narration: Halfway up the stair, the deep sound comes once more, softer, like a sleeper's sigh. The steps shiver. Your copy of the river slides in your pack. "Hold on to it!" Flurry squeaks.
way_out.prompt: Climb the shivering stair without dropping your copy

onSuccess.narration: You climb steady, one hand on your pack. The copy stays safe and dry.

onFailure.narration: The copy slides out and lands in a puddle of meltwater. You snatch it back. The lines run a little, like a picture in the rain, and you bang your knee on a step. But every turn is still there.

ending.narration: At the round glass door, a yeti builder puffs up with frost on his eyebrows. "Flurry! A frost wyrm has curled up in your new room, and it snores snow!" Flurry's knitting drops. The builders' tunnel goes deeper into the glacier; the upper path goes back to the valley. "Now you carry a piece," Murmur whispers. Long ago, this river ran down the valley that was dry, and today it tried to go that way again. The chime still leans down, toward the oldest ice. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Murmur's record has two rivers in it now: this one, and the buried bridge's.
Pip is already writing to Lady Olivia. The letter says RIVERS on the outside.
Pip has written "Ask the river first?" on the cover of his notebook.
Flurry picks up her knitting again. "Then somebody has to go and ask that wyrm to move," she says, and looks at you.
Flurry hides behind Murmur's scarves. "Somebody has to go and look," she squeaks, and looks at you.
